artifact: DiffLocks raw groom v2 for AlpineHero
_adoption_note: Adopted from the operator's Desktop file hero_manual_style_v1.blend. THE FILENAME IS WRONG AND WAS FLAGGED BY THE OPERATOR: it says manual_style_v1 and contains the v2 AI generation. Renamed to hero_v2_generated.blend at intake; the Desktop original is unmodified and hash-equal to the banked copy.

source_blend._object_name_note: The brief called it 'AI Hair Data'. The object is named 'AI Hair'. Names come from the asset, not from the brief.

payload._optimization: operator ran 40% strands / 32 points in the AI panel
payload._transform_note: VERIFIED IDENTITY before seating. The operator flagged that they may have nudged transforms while learning the UI; they did not. Nothing was baked out, so placement remains owned entirely by the registration.
payload.frame: raw DiffLocks, Y-up, metres -- the same convention as v1
payload._frame_conversion: THE IN-BLEND CLOUD WAS ALREADY AXIS-SWAPPED BY THE ADDON. land_difflocks.py applies swap(p)=[x,-z,y] to whatever npz it is given, so banking the blend coordinates directly would swap TWICE -- a 90 degree rotation, which is a symptom this hero has already shown once. extract_strands.py applies the inverse raw=[bx,bz,-by] and ASSERTS the round trip (max err 0.0). Measured evidence for the swap: v1 raw Y [0.169,0.442] lines up with v2 blend Z [0.169,0.432], and v1 raw Z [-0.151,0.127] with v2 blend -Y.
payload._bounds_corroboration: v1 raw was X [-0.110,0.116] Y [0.169,0.442] Z [-0.151,0.127]. Near-identical, which is what a second generation of the same head should look like.
payload._v1_comparison: v1 raw mean 0.0815 m at 256 pts; v2 is slightly longer

lineage._the_caution: The operator's log records a generate_hair() run AFTER the first optimization, so the in-file cloud could have been a different diffusion sample than the server-side outputs.
lineage._how_it_was_settled: ENUMERATED, NOT ASSUMED. The AI panel's server deletes its output directories on shutdown: runtime/outputs/ holds only .aihair_session.json, which reads {'dirs': []}, and a filesystem-wide search found NO .npz, .ply or hair payload written outside this repo on 2026-08-23. There are no server-side outputs to compare against or to archive.
lineage._candidate_detail: The blend holds exactly ONE new CURVES object ('AI Hair', 40281x32). The only other CURVES object is AlpineHero_DiffLocks_v1 (100943x28), which carries groom_root_uv and radius and is the already-seated v1 groom, not a candidate.
lineage._conclusion: One candidate exists anywhere on this machine, so the 'pick whichever the optimized object descends from' question has a single answer by enumeration. NOTHING WAS ARCHIVED AS THE OTHER SAMPLE, because no other sample survives -- stated as an absence found by looking, not as an assumption.
lineage._descends_from: The file itself descends from hero/groomloop/Blender_Test/SOURCE_untouched.blend: it still contains that blend's AlpineHero_DiffLocks_v1 curves, the hero face mesh, the armature, and the HeadCam added by scripts/frame_blend_view.py earlier the same day.
lineage._irreproducible: A generation is a diffusion sample. Re-running the same prompt on the same image yields DIFFERENT strands, so this payload cannot be regenerated and the banked npz is canonical.
